analyst.summary: Coal India had a mixed FY26: production and offtake both missed the company's own targets for a second straight year, and the e-auction premium that drives its best margins nearly halved (69% to 36% year-on-year in Q4), pulling full-year profit down about 12% even though the March quarter alone posted a record number helped partly by non-mining income. Early FY27 volumes are softer still, and a new round of worker wage negotiations (the old 5-year agreement expired end-June 2026) is pending with no date yet - a genuine but un-scheduled cost risk. Against this, the stock trades cheaply (about 8.5 times last year's earnings) with a roughly 6% dividend yield, the company has no financial-stability concerns, and it has a large multi-year plan to diversify into coal gasification, thermal power and critical minerals. We rate it a Hold: the low valuation and dividend already price in the structural slowdown, so it isn't a name we'd flag to sell, but the volume misses, margin volatility and pending wage costs mean it isn't a name to add to on a growth case either.
